notes.title: Retribution Release Date News and Info
notes.notes:
It's good to see you again, Tourists.

With the release of The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners - Chapter 2: Retribution on Meta Headsets, and the launch date announced for PSVR2, players on PC have been waiting to hear news on when the PCVR version of the game would officially launch. We always try to get games in your hands as fast as possible, but sometimes we need to take our time to make sure that your game will work properly and fully utilize the features of your platform of choice. To ensure that the PCVR version of the game looks and runs at the highest possible quality, we've made the decision to move its release from December 2022 to February 2023. We discussed this some days ago, but we should have posted here as well, so sorry for the last minute nature of this post.

We thank you for your patience, and hope to see you return to undead New Orleans in early 2023.

notes.title: New Release Date for Aftershocks + FAQ!
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=djufjNlSABw;full][/previewyoutube]
Thanks for your patience, Tourists.

We know that delays are always tough. For our first simultaneous cross-platform content release, the team has been working hard at getting all versions of the update to live up to our standards.

The good news is that we have a new launch date for Aftershocks, September 23rd!  

The content itself is playable and practically complete, but we are trying to smooth out as many rough edges as we can find. We have been humbled by how many of you have enjoyed the game, and Aftershocks won’t be the end of the content coming to The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners. We will reveal more on this in the coming months.

Still, since September is over a month away, and fans are clamoring to know more about Aftershocks, we thought we would provide an FAQ / feature breakdown to hold you over, and help you prepare for the time being. 

- - -

What exactly is the Aftershocks update?
Aftershocks is the next free update for The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners, expanding the campaign of the game with a new set of post-ending missions, supply caches to find, and a new set of challenges to test your survival skills.

Is it coming to all platforms?
Yes! The Aftershocks update will be coming the same day to all VR platforms that Saints & Sinners has been released on. 

How do I play the new content?
You will have to have reached the ending of the game’s storyline first before the new content unlocks. Once you have officially entered the post-game (i.e. after the credits) keep your radio tuned to channel 47, you may find that it’s worth your while. 

What does the new update include?
Alongside the new missions, the update includes a number of Reserve Caches to find that are filled with late game supplies and unique collectibles, new enemy layouts and scenarios, a new type of environmental hazard to watch out for, and a few extra surprises you’ll find throughout your playthrough. 

Will there be new areas in Aftershocks?
You will be returning to old locations during your time in Aftershocks, but each mission drastically changes, and makes it more challenging, what you’ve grown accustomed to expect. Put simply, the areas are familiar but what you’ll encounter within them won’t be.

Will there be new weapons/items in Aftershocks?
While your walker slaying arsenal won’t be drastically changed by this new update, there may be a new tool that will change the way you interact with the world of Saints & Sinners...beyond that, we can’t say much. 

How Long is the new update?
On a standard playthrough the update should provide around 4 to 6 hours of new content.

How big will the download for the new update be?
The download size for the update will depend on which version of the game you are playing, but our current estimations are as follows...

 PCVR - 31.3GB
 Oculus Quest 1/2 - 6.73GB
 PSVR - 9.67GB
  
More space may be necessary than listed for the initial download, but the total update after installation will be close to the sizes listed above.

When is the Aftershocks update even coming out?
Our new planned release date for the update will be September 23rd, 2021.

notes.title: Release notes for Hotfix #4 - The Walking Dead Saints & Sinners, CL 158675
notes.notes:
Release notes for Hotfix #4 - The Walking Dead Saints & Sinners, CL 158675 

Additions/Improvements:Alpha SteamVR Oculus Support (ini change is required, see the “Hacks” section below)This is an early Work-in-Progress version and there may be some flaws. However, after our initial tests we thought we could share it with now and ask for your help to improve it. Your feedback is always welcomed and is extremely helpful!
Previously unavailable recipes now have a chance to drop from Elite Soldiers during the post game
Increased the Save Slots from 6 to 15 

Bug Fixes: Event System should now continue after completing the game***Note*** We miscommunicated this release note, and we apologize for that! The Event System will work properly for any new game or if it wasn't already broken. If you already have this issue, it will not be fixed. We are looking into a retroactive fix and will keep you posted!
Progression Break - Retroactive fix for “Tomb and the Tower V” (May Intel Quest)If you were already previously stuck on this quest, this should allow you to continue
 
Hacks:To enable Alpha SteamVR Oculus supportAfter downloading the patch, run the game and then exit again
Open your GameUserSettings.ini
Find the block of settings beneath the line (/Script/TWD.TWDGameUserSettings)
Find the entry bEnableOculusSteamVR=False
Change it to bEnableOculusSteamVR=True
Save the file and launch the game again
If your controllers are not working on the Main Menu, the community has mentioned that setting your bindings to default should resolve the issue

notes.title: Release notes for Hotfix #2 - The Walking Dead Saints & Sinners, CL 157393
notes.notes:
For everyone:
 Handgun/Pistol angle adjustments, two-handed grips on one-handed firearms now stay level
...and for those who have demanded it:
 An Alpha version of Physical Crouching!
This an early Work-in-Progress and there are definitely some flaws, but the early results are so promising we wanted to share it now.  Also, we want to ask your help to make it better. So...

The feature is still in active development, and you'll have to hack the INI to expose it.

Here's how: Open your GameUserSettings.ini file which in typical Windows 10 installs will be here:
C:\\Users\\{username}\\AppData\\Local\\TWD\\Saved\\Config\\WindowsNoEditor\\GameUserSettings.ini
Note: The AppData folder may be hidden, but you can reveal it via Folder Options from your Start Menu
 FInd the line that reads: 
/Script/TWD.TWDGameUserSettings
 Right below that, insert the following: bPhysicalCrouchEnabled=True
 Run the game, give it a whirl. 
Some Caveats: Start each play session by hitting ResetHMD/Pause from a comfortable standing position.  If anything gets weird, do it again.
 If you find you have to crouch too far or not far enough you can edit CrouchDistance=32.000 (found in the same file), to any number you find comfortable.  Be sure to post any mods you make that make it feel better.
Known Flaws: Sometimes pops a bit when entering a crawlspace.  We're already working on it. You can find some bits of level geometry that pop you down when you crawl near them.
Post about it!  Tell us what's working and what's not, post videos of awkward moments, or of beautiful ones.  Everything we hear helps us make it better, and believe me we are listening!

Last, we want to give a huge shout-out to everyone who pushed us to make this happen.  You were right - it's going to be amazing!  With your help, we'll get it there.
